rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes continuous loading at elevated temperatures to study creep, while the paper varied the modulation period (λ) of multilayer coatings and used room-temperature nanoindentation creep. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies sustained stress of 100–500 MPa and temperatures of 500–800 °C, whereas the paper used room-temperature nanoindentation with a 5 mN maximum load and loading rates of 1, 0.1, and 0.01 mN/s. The conditions are completely different regimes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a stable surface oxide layer that blocks dislocation movement and grain boundary sliding. The paper's mechanism involves semicoherent interfaces blocking dislocations, leading to interfacial amorphization and a transition to atomic-diffusion or interface-slip creep. These are different classes of mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved creep resistance (reduced steady-state creep rate, increased time to failure) for a coated vs. uncoated baseline. The paper predicts and finds that the λ = 16 nm semicoherent multilayer has the greatest creep resistance and a transition in creep mechanism compared to other modulation periods. The predicted property (creep resistance) and direction (improvement) are the same in general terms, but the specific comparison and outcome details differ.
